record.name: UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision
names: UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision
record.summary: UCSF's Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision at 490 Illinois Street, a 347,500-sq-ft eye-care facility in three buildings (a 12-story tower with a 5-story south wing and a 3-story north wing) that SF YIMBY reported open on November 27, 2020 (SmithGroup architect). The UC Regents approved a $237.13 million total project budget for it in January 2017: "The total project cost of $237.13 million (including $12 million of capitalized interest incurred during construction)"; that is a budget, not a construction cost. It stands on OCII plan block 33, between Third St and Illinois St: the City's address point for 490 Illinois St falls inside this outline, and UCSF's own 2025 campus map labels block 33 'Valley Center for Vision'. Its footprint here is approximate (see the shape's accuracy caveat).

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL BUILDING, APPROXIMATE BOUNDARY -- a real, standing structure clearly visible in Esri satellite imagery (not open land): UCSF's Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision at 490 Illinois St. The City's official address point for 490 Illinois St (DataSF Addresses, address ID 743049, on Assessor parcel 8725001) lies inside this outline; UCSF's June 2025 CAC presentation map labels block 33, between Third St and Illinois St, 'VALLEY CENTER FOR VISION (33)'; and SF YIMBY (2020-11-27) places the facilities 'along 3rd Street, immediately across from the UCSF Medical Center'. Boundary is the edge of the open ground left between the official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes (following the estimated curb radius), with one corner redrawn to the real street angle (see the mapping log), not a hand-traced or surveyed building footprint. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its mapping log. DataSF's Assessor layer has one active lot, 8725001 (480 16th St, MB-RA zoning, recorded 1999-09-21, 15,504 m2), under this building and the two other tracked buildings on this strip between Third St and Illinois St (UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision, UCSF Bayfront Medical Building and UCSF Illinois Street Garage). No lot separates them, so this outline is a drawing of the building from imagery, kept because the lot is not this building's own.
notes.digitized_from: Outlined as the ground left between DataSF's official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes, between 3rd St and Illinois St, south of 16th St. Pier & Point judged that this piece (12,421 sqm before cutting) covers two separate real buildings, not one, and cut it by hand at the visible gap between the two rooflines in Esri satellite imagery (lat 37.76578).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The strip holds one Assessor lot, 8725001, under three separately drawn buildings (see the accuracy note), so no lot of its own exists for this building.

costs.what: Total project budget for the Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision (Block 33), as approved by the UC Regents; it includes $12 million of capitalized interest incurred during construction, so it is not a construction cost

milestones.text: The UC Regents, at their January 26, 2017 meeting, approve a $237.13 million project budget and the design of the Mission Bay East Campus Phase 1 Building (Block 33) at UCSF Mission Bay: a 12-story tower with a 5-story south wing, which the Regents' committee was told would house the Center for Vision and Neurological Sciences, and a 3-story north wing. The Regents' documents do not use the name Valley Center for Vision. The agenda item gave a proposed schedule of completion by July 2019, with construction starting in June 2017

changes.text: UCSF's Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision at 490 Illinois St is the block 33 building between Third St and Illinois St, not the pair of buildings east of Illinois St that this project had listed under that name. The City's address point for 490 Illinois St falls inside the block 33 outline; UCSF's 2025 campus map labels block 33 'Valley Center for Vision'; SF YIMBY places the facility 'along 3rd Street, immediately across from the UCSF Medical Center'; and the two buildings east of Illinois St were already standing, about six stories tall, in the City's 2010 building survey. The block 33 record is renamed 'UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision' and now carries the 2017 Regents approval, the November 2020 opening, the $237 million cost, the SmithGroup design, the 347,500 sq ft size and the Caffe Central tenant. Its old page address redirects to the new one.

open_questions: No source read gives the exact opening day: SF YIMBY reported the building open on November 27, 2020, without a date.

The Regents' January 2017 documents describe the proposed Block 33 building as 343,000 gross square feet (275,400 assignable), mainly academic and administrative workspace (200,500 assignable square feet) with 45,200 assignable square feet of vision clinic space. SF YIMBY's 347,500 square feet at opening is a different figure, and no source read explains the difference.

No opening date was found for Caffe Central at 490 Illinois St: the cafe's own page (Caffe Central, '490 Illinois Street -- Mission Bay') lists the location and its hours (Monday-Friday 7am-4pm) but gives no date.

OpenStreetMap labels one of the 409/499 Illinois St buildings across Illinois St (way 84821722; tags addr:housenumber 490, addr:street Illinois Street, building:levels 6, height 28) as 490 Illinois St. The City's address point, UCSF's 2025 campus map and SF YIMBY's description all place the 12-story Valley Center for Vision here instead, so that label is not used.

Geometry: this building's east edge sits close to, but not necessarily exactly on, Illinois St's west curb line; it has not been checked against a building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, surveyed in 2010, predates the building).
